deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematical derivation. It is a passage of Riemann's natural-philosophical notes, his reaction to Fechner's 'Zend-Avesta' and the Erdseele (earth-soul) doctrine, followed by the start of his physical speculation on the ether.

(1) It ends the argument from the previous page on 'whether' (über das Ob) a unified thinking process in the Earth must be assumed. Purposiveness in organisms finds its closure in the Earth, for three reasons:
- (b1) All organisms are made for life on the Earth's crust, so the state of the crust contains all (external) grounds of their constitution.
- (b2) The organic arrangements are individual. By all experience they do not repeat on other celestial bodies.
- (b3) They do not stay fixed over the Earth's life. Ever more perfect organisms appear. So the cause must be a simultaneous thinking process that advances to higher stages.

Conclusion: from the standpoint of exact natural science (explanation of nature from causes), the earth-soul is a hypothesis to explain the existence and historical development of the organic world.

(2) 'Über das Wie' (on the 'how'):
- Thinking is a process inside ponderable matter.
- The external facts that must be explained by processes inside ponderable (gravitating) matter are (1) universal gravitation and (2) the general laws of motion.
- Every act of thought leaves something permanent (shown only through memory) that exerts no lasting influence on phenomena.
- Conversely, our external experience of ponderable matter is explained if a homogeneous substance fills all infinite space, flows continually into ponderable matter, and vanishes there. This is Riemann's well-known 'Stoff' that enters ponderable atoms and passes into the mental world; it is the published sink hypothesis of gravitation.

After a gap ('Lücke'): the actions of ponderable matter on ponderable matter are (1) attractive and repulsive forces inversely proportional to the square of the distance, and (2) light and radiant heat. Both classes are to be explained by a space-filling homogeneous substance; the sentence continues on the next page with local action only.

My modern gloss, not on the page: an incompressible medium flowing into a point sink of strength Q has radial velocity v(r) = -Q/(4*pi*r**2). It is divergence-free away from the sink, giving an inverse-square law. This is the standard reconstruction of Riemann's 1853 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie'. No formula appears here.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no computation. Philosophically, the step from 'cause of purposiveness not found in a larger whole' to 'a single Earth thinking-process' is a hypothesis, which Riemann himself labels as such.

results.what: Earth-soul (Erdseele) as an explanatory hypothesis for the existence and progressive development of organic life
results.usually_credited_to: G. T. Fechner (Zend-Avesta, 1851); Riemann's critique is published in his Werke, 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts'

results.what: Space filled with a homogeneous substance that flows into ponderable matter and vanishes there, explaining gravitation (inverse-square forces) and light/heat by local action
results.modern_name: Ether sink/flow theory of gravitation; field-theoretic local-action ether
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1853 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie', published 1876 in Werke); similar ideas in Euler and later Bjerknes and Yarkovsky

deep.surprise_reason: This is part of Riemann's known and published natural-philosophical fragments (Werke 1876/1892). The ether-sink gravitation idea and the Fechner discussion are well documented. The pencil note 'Schluss. (Von hier an weggelassen)' appears to be an editor's mark of where the printed excerpt stops, which is a minor editorial detail.

checkable.asserts: Radial inflow to a point sink in an incompressible medium is divergence-free for r>0, with speed proportional to 1/r**2. This is the modern gloss of the inverse-square law from the sink hypothesis, not on the page.
Flux through any sphere around the sink equals the constant sink strength Q (mass conservation underlying the inverse-square dependence).
